notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its meetings of 1994, from volume 40 of the San Francisco Public Library's deposit at the Internet Archive (40minutesofsanfran1994san). By 1994 the minutes are action minutes: each calendar item prints its case number and planner, the property with its assessor's block and lot, the request, the speakers by name, and the action with the vote and the motion or resolution number; there is no staff report and no debate. Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false, and every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the calendar states stood on or occupied the property; one dated past fact; and landmark actions. A continuance, a withdrawal or a motion of intent is not a decision; a Board of Permit Appeals or Board of Supervisors action reported without its own date takes the reporting meeting's date and an 'By ... had' frame. The minutes name applicants, owners, architects, neighbours, objectors, commissioners and staff in every item; the reader spec barred all of them from every field and kept companies, institutions, businesses and named buildings.

coverage.remaining: Every page of volume 40 (40minutesofsanfran1994san, labelled 1994) was read: 30 meetings, 6 January to 17 November 1994 (29 regular and the joint special meeting of 28 April with the Recreation and Park Commission, whose minutes are bound twice). The volume holds no minutes for 5, 19 and 26 May, any meeting of June or July, 10 November or December; 31 March, 7 April and 15 September were cancelled. 28 April's regular meeting is bound twice (final and draft); the final was used. Next: volumes 41-58 (1995-2005), which are the same kind of action minutes and can be sized by text pages.
coverage.note: 199 OCR pages with text out of 220 viewer pages (222 scanned leaves; the empty ones are versos, the library card and the digitization notice), read in one session by a single reader with no sub-agents. The year is the year of the Residential Conservation Controls fight, of the Tier III informational calendar that put dozens of rear decks and additions before the Commission, of the Civic Center courts building and the State office building, of the Cornell Hotel's refused tourist-hotel conversion, and of Balboa High School's landmark recommendation.
